S8.01.needs: a chat with a sent message
S8.01.note: The primary style comes from packages/ui/ui/src/primitives/Button.tsx (default variant).
steps: Open a chat that has a message you sent.
Hover your sent message and click the pencil button labelled Edit message.
Change the text and look for the Save & Retry button.
Compare: it should look like the main filled action, with a readable label.
S8.01.where: Chat > hover your sent message > Edit message (pencil) > Save & Retry

S8.02.note: Outline button found in ComposerFeedbackDialog, but I did not trace how a person opens that dialog, and no other outline button was confirmed.

S8.03.needs: a chat with shared links, so the button appears
S8.03.note: Revoke every link shows only when the share inventory is incomplete (inventoryIncomplete); the title-menu trigger itself was not traced.
steps: Open a chat and open its title menu, then choose Share….
Look for the Revoke every link button in the dialog footer.
Compare: it should be styled as a red destructive button with readable text.
Do not click it unless you are ready to revoke links.
S8.03.where: Share… (chat title menu) > Revoke every link

S8.04.needs: a chat with a sent message
S8.04.note: The icon buttons appear for your own messages only when a retry or edit handler exists.
steps: Open a chat and hover over a message you sent.
Look for the small icon buttons that appear: Retry this message and Edit message.
Hover each one to see its tooltip (Retry, Edit).
Compare: each icon button should have a name for screen readers and a tooltip.
S8.04.where: Chat > hover your sent message > icon button Retry this message

S8.06.note: The pressed state (aria-pressed) appears only when some attachment or tool is active; the button label changes to a count when there are active items.
steps: Open a chat and look at the message box at the bottom.
Click the + button.
Look at whether the + button shows a pressed state and the menu opens.
Compare: the button should report pressed or expanded state, and its count badge shows active items.

S8.07.note: The microphone button label was not traced; the group label is read from the strip's code.
steps: Start voice dictation from the message box.
Look at the strip that appears next to the composer.
Hover or tab through its two round buttons.
Compare: the strip should be one labelled group with a cancel (discard) button.
S8.07.where: Composer > dictation (microphone) button > the Voice dictation strip

S8.08.needs: a reply that contains a link
S8.08.note: Link text depends on the reply; no fixed label exists in code.
steps: Send a message that asks for a web page or source.
Find a link inside the assistant's reply.
Click the link.
Compare: it should look like a link and open its destination.
S8.08.where: Chat > any assistant reply that contains a web link > click the link

S8.09.note: Single-line input found in CreateProjectDialog, but I did not trace how a person opens that dialog.

S8.10.note: The new-line key was not confirmed in code; the feedback dialog also has a multi-line Details box, but its open path was not traced.
steps: Open a chat and click into the message box.
Type a line, then add a new line.
Compare: the box should accept several lines and grow taller as you type.
S8.10.where: Chat > the message box at the bottom of the screen

S8.11.note: The model picker button that opens this catalogue was not traced.
steps: Open the model picker in the message box area.
Click the Search models field.
Type part of a model name.
Compare: the list should narrow to matching models.

S8.12.note: Masked password field found in ConnectorApiKeyForm, but the screen path that shows this form was not traced.

S8.13.needs: an email sign-in that asks for a code
S8.13.note: AuthCodeStep.tsx has a numeric one-time-code field (autocomplete one-time-code), but the sign-in path that shows it was not traced.

S8.14.note: The Export menu item text was not traced; the checkbox only shows when the chosen format supports metadata.
steps: Open a chat and open its title menu.
Choose Export.
Look for the checkbox Include metadata (title, date, message count) and click it.
Compare: the box should toggle and its checked state should change.
S8.14.where: Chat title menu > Export (opens Export Chat History) > Include metadata checkbox

labels.text: What do you want to do first?

S8.15.needs: a new account that sees onboarding
S8.15.note: The question is screen-reader only (sr-only), so a sighted person may not see the words.
steps: Start the onboarding wizard on first sign-in, or reopen it.
Look at the group of choices for what you want to do first.
Click one choice and check that only that choice is selected.
Compare: only one option is selected at a time.

S8.16.needs: a model that supports extended thinking
S8.16.note: The switch shows only for models with thinking support; the toggle label is an aria-label, not visible text.
steps: Click the reasoning or Effort control in the message box.
Look at the Effort row in the popover.
Click the switch and watch it turn on or off.
Compare: the switch should change state immediately.
S8.16.where: Composer > Effort (reasoning button) > Toggle extended thinking switch

S8.17.note: Both segments are icon-only; the label text comes from aria-label, so no visible words to quote.
steps: Open the Code screen.
Look at the small two-part control at the top of the side rail.
Click the chat icon and check that the chat screen opens.
Compare: the active part should look selected.
S8.17.where: Code screen > top of the left rail > two-part icon control (chat icon and code icon)

S8.18.note: How global search opens was not traced.
steps: Open global search from the app.
Look for the Message Type field with its value (all, user, assistant, system).
Pick one value and check the list narrows.
Compare: exactly one value should be selected.

S8.19.note: Searchable combobox found in CommandPalette.tsx; the keyboard shortcut or menu that opens it was not traced.

S8.20.note: The panel uses a checkbox menu, not chips; no clear several-value chip list was confirmed, and the Changes panel path was not traced.

labels.text: Press Enter or type a comma to add an entry.

S8.21.note: The Workspace policy screen path was not traced; the field label is an aria label in the code.
steps: Open the workspace policy section as a workspace admin.
Click into the IP allow list field and type an address, then press Enter.
Look for the new chip and its remove control.
Compare: the entry should appear as a removable chip.
S8.21.where: Workspace settings > Workspace policy > IP allow list field (Add an IP address or CIDR block)

S8.22.needs: a Free or paid account with Schedules
S8.22.note: The button that opens the new schedule form was not traced.
steps: Open the Schedules page and start a new schedule.
Find Repeat Every and click its up and down arrows, or type a number.
Compare: the value should go up and down by one and stay at least 1.
Check the helper text below it.
S8.22.where: Schedules > new schedule form > Repeat Every field

S8.23.needs: a model that supports several effort levels
S8.23.note: The slider appears only when the model offers more than one effort level.
steps: Click the reasoning control in the message box.
Find the Effort row and drag the slider.
Try the arrow keys after clicking the slider.
Compare: the value changes between effort levels.
S8.23.where: Composer > Effort (reasoning button) > slider under the Effort label

S8.25.note: How global search opens was not traced.
steps: Open global search.
Click the Select date button for the start date.
Pick a day in the calendar and check the button shows that date.
Compare: the calendar should close and the chosen date should show.
S8.25.where: Global search dialog > Start date > Select date

S8.26.needs: a schedule form that shows Local Time
S8.26.note: The button that opens the new schedule form was not traced.
steps: Open the new schedule form and choose a daily, weekly or monthly repeat.
Find the Local Time field.
Click it and set a time.
Compare: the chosen time should show in the field.
S8.26.where: Schedules > new schedule form > Local Time field

S8.27.note: The button that opens the new schedule form was not traced; the list uses a datalist.
steps: Open the new schedule form.
Click the Time Zone field and type a city or region.
Pick a suggested zone from the list.
Compare: the field should show the picked zone and default to the device zone.
S8.27.where: Schedules > new schedule form > Time Zone field

S8.28.note: The Settings panel with this tab is the desktop Local-mode SettingsPanel; the Cloud mode uses the shared SettingsModal, which I did not trace. A second colour input exists on the project page (aria-label 'Custom colour', no visible text) at apps/web/app/chat/projects/[id]/page.tsx.
steps: Open Settings and choose Appearance.
Scroll to the Themes heading and click Create Theme.
In Create Custom Theme, click the small colour square next to Background.
Look for a colour chooser that opens and changes the swatch and the hex text beside it.
S8.28.where: Settings > Appearance > Themes > Create Theme (the colour squares next to Background, Foreground and the other colour names in the Create Custom Theme dialog)

S8.29.note: The add-button visible text was not checked; its aria-label comes from packages/ui/i18n/locales/en/chat.json key composer.addAttachmentsAndTools.
steps: Open a chat and click the add button at the bottom-left of the composer.
Click Add photos & files.
Choose a file in the system file chooser and confirm.
Look for the chosen file to appear as a preview above the message box.
S8.29.where: Chat composer > the add button (aria-label 'Add attachments and tools') > Add photos & files; or the composer Files menu > Upload from device

labels.text: Release to attach to your message

S8.30.needs: a file to upload, a mouse or trackpad drag
steps: Open a chat in the desktop app.
Drag a file from Finder over the chat window and hold it there.
Look for the overlay with the heading Drop files here and the line Release to attach to your message.
Release the file and check it appears as an attachment in the composer.
S8.30.where: Chat > drag a file from Finder over the chat window (the composer area)

S8.31.needs: a chat with a research or web-sources answer
S8.31.note: The tablist has the accessible name Research views; the Globe button label comes from ResearchPanel.tsx.
steps: Open a chat that produced research sources.
Click the button with the title Research sources to open the panel.
Click the Report tab, then the Library tab.
Look for the selected tab to change and for the panel content to switch with it.
S8.31.where: Chat > after an answer with web research, click the Globe button titled Research sources > tabs Sources, Report, Library

S8.32.needs: a chat where the model returns a steps card (not directly controllable by the tester)
S8.32.note: Whether a steps card appears depends on the model output; the tester cannot force one from a button.
steps: Open a chat that returns a steps card.
Click a step row or its arrow.
Look for the details to open below the step and the arrow state to change.
Click again and check the details close.
S8.32.where: Chat > a reply shown as a steps card > click a step row to expand its details

S8.33.needs: a model that returns thinking steps
S8.33.note: The button is shown only when the reply has thinking steps.
steps: Open a chat whose reply includes thinking steps.
Click Thinking process under the reply.
Look for the list of thinking steps to open and the arrow to turn down.
Click again and check the list closes.
S8.33.where: Chat > a reply with thinking steps > the button Thinking process (N steps) under the reply

S8.34.note: Add chat instructions appears only when the onEditInstructions handler is passed.
steps: Open any saved chat.
Click the chat title at the top with its small down arrow.
Look for a menu with Rename and Add chat instructions or Edit chat instructions.
Press the down arrow key, then Escape, and check the menu closes and focus returns to the title.
S8.34.where: Chat > click the conversation title at the top (aria-label Conversation options) > menu items Rename, Add chat instructions

S8.36.note: The item is hidden when there are no projects.
steps: Open a saved chat and click its title to open the menu.
Hover or click Move to project.
Look for a submenu listing your projects.
Click a project name and check the chat moves into it (the item changes to Change project).
S8.36.where: Chat > click the conversation title > Move to project (opens a submenu of projects)

S8.37.needs: a sent message in a chat
steps: Open a chat and find one of your sent messages.
Move the mouse onto the pencil icon under it, or focus it with the keyboard.
Look for a small label Edit to appear.
Move the mouse away and check the label goes away.
S8.37.where: Chat > hover over the pencil icon (aria-label Edit message) under one of your sent messages

S8.38.note: The visible text of the trigger button was not found; only its aria-label Files was located.
steps: Open a chat and click the composer Files button.
Look for a floating panel above the composer with a search field and Upload from device.
Press Escape, and check the panel closes.
Open it again, click outside it, and check it closes.
S8.38.where: Chat > composer Files menu (trigger aria-label Files) > panel with Search library files and Upload from device

S8.39.note: The chip's aria-label is a template; the visible chip text was not found in code.
steps: Open a chat with a web-search answer that shows source chips.
Hover over a source chip.
Look for a card listing the source rows with the site name and a snippet.
Move the mouse away and check the card closes.
S8.39.where: Chat > an answer with web citations > hover a small source chip under the answer

S8.40.note: The badge count is code-driven; I did not locate other badges in the StepsCard header.
steps: Open a chat with research sources and keep the sources panel closed.
Look at the Globe button in the top bar.
Check for a small count bubble on its corner.
Open the panel and check the bubble disappears.
S8.40.where: Chat > Research sources button (Globe icon) > count badge when sources exist and the panel is closed

S8.41.needs: a chat with a calculation answer
S8.41.note: CalculationCard renders the unit as a Badge with dynamic text (apps/web/features/chat/components/cards/CalculationCard.tsx line 169-177), with no fixed visible label. I could not confirm this is a distinct tag rather than a status badge.

S8.42.needs: a screen reader for the accessible-label step
S8.42.note: apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/MessageBubble.tsx says the web chat shows no avatars, so the distinction is by layout and the hidden heading, not a picture.
steps: Open a chat with one message from you and one reply.
Look for the two messages to look different (your message in a bubble, the reply as plain text).
Turn on VoiceOver and move through the two messages; check each is announced with You said: or Assistant said:.
S8.42.where: Chat transcript: your messages sit in a bubble, assistant replies are plain text; screen readers hear You said: and Assistant said:

S8.43.needs: a steps card in a chat
S8.43.note: The steps card depends on model output; the loading spinner shows only briefly.
steps: Open a chat that returns a steps card.
Tick off steps and watch the progress bar and the text N% complete.
Check the text changes to All steps completed! when all are done.
Open a chat and watch for the loading spinner labelled Loading chat.
S8.43.where: Chat > a steps card > progress bar and percent text under its title; the loading spinner appears when a chat opens

S8.44.needs: a saved chat and a slow connection
S8.44.note: Placeholder text is not visible; the skeleton component is apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/MessageBubbleSkeleton.tsx. Visibility is brief.
steps: Throttle the network in the browser developer tools if available, or use a slow connection.
Open a saved chat.
Look for grey animated placeholder message bubbles before the real messages appear.
Check the placeholders are replaced by the real messages.
S8.44.where: Chat > open a conversation on a slow connection; grey placeholder message bubbles show before the messages load

labels.text: Could not save the model for this conversation. The previous model remains active.

S8.45.needs: a way to make the save fail (network off)
S8.45.note: The toast shows only when the model save fails; the desktop copy is Could not save this conversation’s model. Try again. in apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx.
steps: Open a chat and turn off the network connection.
Open the model picker in the composer and choose a different model.
Look for the error toast with the message about the model not being saved.
Wait a few seconds and check the toast goes away on its own.
S8.45.where: Chat > composer model picker > choose another model while the save fails (toast at the bottom)

labels.text: Couldn't load this conversation. Check your connection and try again.

S8.46.needs: a way to make a turn fail (network off)
S8.46.note: The exact alert text depends on the failure; the alert role is set on TranscriptNotice in apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx near line 6888 and the banner at line 7556.
steps: Open a chat and send a message while the network is off.
Look for a red alert block in the conversation with an explanation.
Check that the alert offers a recovery action where one applies (for example a retry link).
S8.46.where: Chat > a turn that fails shows an inline alert in the transcript with a recovery action

labels.text: Get notified when the response is ready.

S8.47.needs: a long reply and notification permission not yet granted
S8.47.note: The dismiss button text was not located.
steps: Open a chat in a browser that has not granted notifications.
Send a message that takes a while to answer.
Look for the strip Get notified when the response is ready. with an Enable button.
Click Enable or the dismiss control and check the strip reacts.
S8.47.where: Chat > send a long message > the strip at the top of the chat: Get notified when the response is ready. with Enable

S8.48.needs: an account with more projects than one page
S8.48.note: Sidebar label for the Projects entry was not verified.
steps: Open Projects from the sidebar.
Scroll to the bottom of the list.
Click Show more.
Look for the Loading projects text while loading, then more projects appear.
S8.48.where: Projects > the Projects list at the bottom > Show more

S8.49.needs: an account or chat with no artifacts
S8.49.note: The control that opens the Artifacts panel was not located.
steps: Open a chat with no artifacts.
Open the Artifacts panel.
Look for the empty message No artifacts yet with the line Renderable code and generated files will appear here.
S8.49.where: Chat > Artifacts panel with no artifacts yet

S8.50.needs: a way to make the list fail (network off)
S8.50.note: Chat-level error text is Couldn't load this conversation. Check your connection and try again. (apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx).
steps: Open Projects while the network is off or the list cannot load.
Look for the error message and the Retry button.
Turn the network back on, click Retry, and check the list loads.
S8.50.where: Projects > the Projects list fails to load > Retry
